title: Dùghall Garbh dies of his wound
summary: Dùghall Garbh dies at Baile Mòr dhomhain of a cut taken below the arm at Muileann chrom that he hid from his own physicians for days. Catrìona nic Aonghais rides three days to reach him and finds him already dead, his last words asking only whether Taigh na Fèithe gates stood open.

title: Dùghall's captains come over unbidden
summary: Dùghall Garbh's captains, led by Artair mac Lachlainn, come to Catrìona's camp within the fortnight and lay no terms before her, saying only that their dead lord had told them what he meant to do if the battle at Muileann chrom went their way, and that his word binds them still.

title: Catrìona crowned at An Talla Dearg
summary: Catrìona nic Aonghais is crowned at Cathair dhearg with little ceremony, the crown itself sent down under guard from Taigh na Fèithe's own custody. The seven heads swear to her in the old order, and she is called Catrìona Bhuadhach from that year.

title: Eòghann keeps Raghnall's list unscraped
summary: Eòghann mac Dhùghaill, still master of the store at Taigh na Fèithe, leaves Raghnall Ruadh's list of refused hearths standing face to the wall in the storeroom and sends word, unasked, that the store will not go a season again without measuring the handful while he holds the beam.

title: The drafting of Riaghailt an Teallaich
summary: At Taigh na Fèithe's own yard Catrìona and the seven heads of the houses spend three days drafting one sentence binding any claimant, house or king from ever again withholding the measured handful. Eòghann mac Dhùghaill is called to testify what Raghnall Ruadh said to him, and his flat account settles the argument the queen's own words could not.

title: The seven heads set their marks
summary: Riaghailt an Teallaich is entered into Leabhar a' Chùraim beside Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig in the same hand, and the seven heads of the houses set their marks to it one after another, Beathag nic Uisdein of Clann Ìomhair last and longest over her own mark.

title: Seònaid nic Coinnich comes to An Talla Dearg
summary: Seònaid nic Coinnich, whose father Coinneach mac Ailein came through the winter of the refusal with a cough he never lost, walks up from Cathair mhòr to An Talla Dearg and is taken into the queen's household as a clerk, the first of several children of the cold shires the household shelters in those years.

title: Seònaid copies the tallies of the refusal
summary: In her first winter at An Talla Dearg, Seònaid nic Coinnich asks to see Leabhar a' Chùraim's oldest entries and copies out, unbidden, the tallies of the hearths refused in the winter of Na Teallaichean Fuara, a labour the queen never questions when she comes upon it by lamplight.

title: Death of Iain mac Eachainn
summary: Iain mac Eachainn, the queen's husband, dies of a wasting in the chest no physician of the household can name. He had kept, through his years in An Talla Dearg, to the smaller business of the household and left the crown's affairs to Catrìona.

title: The council questions Rathad na Banrighinn
summary: More than one head of house asks Catrìona in open council why she spends so much of the treasury on a stone road to her own town of Inis thais. She answers that a kingdom bound by a law written in a cold yard ought to be bound also by roads a hard winter cannot cut, and the building goes on.

title: Rathad na Banrighinn laid to Inis thais
summary: The stone of Rathad na Banrighinn is finished south from the capital, past Am Buabhall Fortanach at Doire shean, all the way to Catrìona's own gate at Inis thais, which she has ridden the length of twice while it was building to feel whether the stone held.

title: The first carters run Rathad na Banrighinn
summary: Salt-carts and grain-carts run the full length of the new stone road within the year the last stone is laid, cutting the journey from three days to two. An old carter tells the household he drove it half-blind and felt the cart go steady the whole way, a thing the mire road never let him do.

title: Seann Warr's grant cut over the gate
summary: In memory of its standing aside through the war and the two sieges it withstood, Catrìona grants Seann Warr the right to keep its own gates and take its own tolls, and the grant is cut in stone letters over the landward gate.

title: Death of Catrìona Bhuadhach
summary: Catrìona Bhuadhach dies at Cathair dhearg at seventy-eight, the last ruler to have fought in Cogadh nan Trì Tagraichean. Her son Lachlann mac Iain, not yet forty, succeeds her.

title: Na Seachd Taighean swear in a single day
summary: The seven heads of the houses swear to Lachlann mac Iain within a single day of his mother's burial, Beathag nic Uisdein of Clann Ìomhair first to kneel. Seònaid nic Coinnich, watching from the back of the hall, counts the swearings without meaning to and goes that evening to begin the opening words of her history of the war.

title: Birth of Lachlann mac Iain
summary: A son, Lachlann, is born at Cathair dhearg to Queen Catrìona Bhuadhach, nine-and-thirty years old and three years crowned, and her husband Iain mac Eachainn.

title: Birth of Anna
summary: A daughter, Anna, is born at Cathair dhearg to Lachlann mac Iain, the queen's son, then five-and-thirty; the old queen, seventy-four, lives to see her granddaughter walk.
